clue.text: Loki, say, second across river at rear of boat, almost

indicators.note: the river letter lies across, so sits inside, the word for a second

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: the stern is the back end of a boat

explanation.surface: A Norse god straddles a river near the back of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loki, say' looks like it wants a god's name, but the definition is the general type he exemplifies, a deceiver.
explanation.definitionFit: Loki is the Norse god of mischief, the classic example of a deceiver who plays pranks.

clue.text: Poet brooded over note to singers

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a hen sat on eggs when it brooded
so (soh) is a note in the tonic sol-fa used by singers

explanation.surface: A poet mulled over a message for the choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was an Italian Renaissance poet, author of Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: As a joke, say, start to analyse food consumed

indicators.note: say means the phrase is heard, giving a sound alike with different spelling

parts.note: in jest means as a joke

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word analyse

explanation.surface: Jokingly, begin to examine what you've eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: IN JEST spoken sounds like INGEST; the A from 'analyse' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingesta is the technical term for material taken into the body as nourishment.

clue.text: Move vessel across present lake, showing practical skill

indicators.note: the vessel-moving word lies across, so surrounds, the other letters

parts.note: to kedge is to move a ship by hauling on a small anchor
now means the present moment

explanation.surface: Steering a boat over a lake shows expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: KEDGE is a nautical term: to warp a ship along by a light anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge includes practical know-how, the skill learned through experience.

clue.text: What's-his-name's light adhesive — a shilling

parts.note: thin, as in thin air, can mean light
gum is a glue
bob is slang for a shilling, an old British coin worth twelve pence

explanation.surface: Someone's flimsy glue cost a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob is the slang name for the pre-1971 British shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingumabob is a placeholder name used when you cannot recall what someone or something is called.

clue.text: Cereal that's twisted, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak means spoken out, a sound alike

parts.note: wry means twisted or distorted, as a wry face

explanation.surface: A grain that is bent, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a grain crop used for bread and whisky.

clue.text: Material from reef originally surrounded by blackish rock

indicators.note: the first letter of reef is surrounded by, so placed inside, the rock word

parts.note: coal is a black sedimentary rock

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word reef

explanation.surface: A substance taken from a reef is enclosed by dark stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material from reef' looks like the whole definition, but 'reef' supplies only its R, which goes inside COAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a hard substance used for jewellery and ornaments, so it counts as a material.

clue.text: Greek character throwing over a new mate

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: throwing over means turning these letters back to front

explanation.surface: A Greek man dumps his partner for a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing over' reverses A and N to NA. China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china, from china plate, means mate or friend.

clue.text: Wine served in front of express trains on the move

indicators.note: on the move means the letters are set moving, rearranged
front of points to the first letter of the word express

explanation.surface: Drink served in the dining car at the front of a fast train.
explanation.walkthrough: The E from 'express' joins TRAINS, and 'on the move' shuffles them all.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Civic dignitary spreads goodness right across county

indicators.note: spreads means the outer pieces are stretched round another
across says these pieces lie over the county, enclosing it

parts.note: Lord! is an exclamation of surprise like goodness!
Mayo is a county in Ireland

explanation.surface: A town dignitary spreads goodwill and justice through the county.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces split around the county name, one at each end; MAYO is a county in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord mayor is the ceremonial head of a major city council.

clue.text: Retired soldiers rejected smooth Italians

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the soldiers word is read backwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for smooth is reversed

parts.note: to iron is to smooth out creases

explanation.surface: Veteran troops were turned away by suave men from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns GIS into SIG; 'rejected' turns IRON into NORI.
explanation.definitionFit: Signori is the Italian plural for gentlemen, so it names Italian men.

clue.text: One who boots out European champion

parts.note: a victor is a winner, a champion

explanation.surface: A champion from Europe is the one who kicks people out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who evicts tenants is ejecting them from a property, booting them out.

clue.text: Singer removing car from roundabout

indicators.note: removing signals that the letters of the car are taken out

parts.note: a carousel is a fairground roundabout, a merry-go-round
the word car taken as written

explanation.surface: A vocalist takes a car off a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: A roundabout here is the fairground ride (CAROUSEL), not the traffic circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is a songbird such as the blackbird; crosswords often call birds singers.

clue.text: Where energetic people may be employed in the vaults?

definitions.text: Where energetic people may be employed in the vaults?

parts.words: Where energetic people may be employed in the vaults?
parts.note: vaults suggest cellars or crypts, but here they are the leaps over a vaulting horse done by athletes

explanation.surface: A guess about who works down in the cellars.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym is a hall for exercise where gymnasts perform vaults over the horse.

clue.text: Doctor caught mixing big drink for winger

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: mixing signals that the letters of big drink are stirred up

explanation.surface: A medic was caught concocting a large cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: The mockingbird is an American songbird; crosswords use winger for any bird.

clue.text: She's a duck, some say

indicators.note: some say means it is the pronunciation of some speakers, without a sounded R

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck

explanation.surface: A woman is described as a duck by certain people.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-rhotic speakers say EIDER without the final R, matching the girl's name Ida.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is a woman's name, so a crossword can define it simply as a female person.

clue.text: On the rocks off Hampshire, holed by prow of vessel?

indicators.note: holed by means pierced, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: the Solent is the strait off the Hampshire coast, so off Hampshire is in the Solent

indicators.note: prow of means the front letter of the word vessel

explanation.surface: A ship aground off the south coast, holed at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off Hampshire' reads as IN SOLENT; the Solent is the stretch of sea between Hampshire and the Isle of Wight. V goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: On the rocks is an idiom for broke, financially ruined, unable to pay debts.

clue.text: Girl hugging numbers of Romans after party in the home

indicators.note: after places the girl's name, with its contents, behind the party word

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: hugging means the girl's name wraps round the numerals

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
I, CI and LI are Roman numerals for one, 101 and 51

explanation.surface: A girl clutching Latin figures after a party at somebody's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman numerals are one, 101 and 51 run together; the M at the front belongs to the girl's name, not the numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Domiciliary means relating to or taking place in a person's house, as in domiciliary care.

clue.text: Homeliest resort, showing flexibility

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, means sort the letters again

explanation.surface: The cosiest holiday spot proves supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithesome means lithe, supple and agile in movement.

clue.text: Revolutionary priest set out to bury doctor

indicators.note: to bury means the doctor letters are put deep inside the mixed letters
out signals that the letters of priest and set are rearranged

parts.note: MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A priest sets out to bury a medic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a verb, but it is part of the fodder; the 'out' shuffle gives SEPTERIST, which the doctor letters split.
explanation.definitionFit: A Septembrist was one of those behind the September massacres of 1792 in revolutionary France.

clue.text: Effect of subsidence, even if limited by staff

indicators.note: limited by means bounded on each side by the staff word

parts.note: a pole is a staff or stick
tho, short for though, means even if

explanation.surface: Sinking ground, even when held back by supports.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a hollow in a road surface, often caused by ground sinking.

clue.text: Old man beginning to relish equality

parts.note: pa, like old man, is an informal word for father

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word relish

explanation.surface: An elderly man starts to enjoy being equal.
explanation.definitionFit: Par means a level of equality, as in being on a par with someone.

clue.text: Church dignitary not yet dead, do we infer?

parts.note: pre means before, a time not yet reached
late means deceased, as in the late king

explanation.surface: A bishop still alive, so one might deduce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do we infer?' playfully treats the word as before (PRE) late (dead).
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a senior churchman such as a bishop or archbishop.

clue.text: Antisocial person's complaint in breeding-kennels?

definitions.meaning: someone who drops rubbish in public places
an illness, or bug, afflicting a litter of puppies

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits into LITTER (a brood of puppies) and BUG (an illness).
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug is someone who leaves rubbish lying about in public, an inconsiderate person.

clue.text: English chap abandoning mother's code of living

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving out the mother letters from the chap's name

parts.note: Thomas is a man's name, any chap
ma is mother

explanation.surface: An Englishman leaves his mother's moral code behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is a link (mother is); the mother letters come out of the chap's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the guiding spirit or set of beliefs of a person or community.

clue.text: Press chief engages male staff to do it

definitions.text: Press chief engages male staff to do it

indicators.note: engages means the chief takes the staff in, enclosing them

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief at a newspaper
men are male workers, a staff of males

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor hires men to do the correcting.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes an editor hiring men to correct copy, which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct a text, the very task an editor hires staff to perform.

clue.text: Gloomy king in costly raiment?

indicators.note: in means the king letter is placed inside, as if dressed in finery

parts.note: dear means expensive
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch dressed in expensive robes looks glum.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers 'raiment': R is clothed in DEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic word for dreary, dismal and dull.

clue.text: Like world-shaking events rocking old chapel

indicators.note: rocking means shaking up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Momentous events are shaking an ancient chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochal describes something so momentous that it marks the start of a new era.

clue.text: Jailbird getting the wind up endlessly

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A convict gets nervous, without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts GALE to GAL; 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lag, or old lag, is British slang for a convict.

clue.text: Cut off current roofing material, having received nothing

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: having received means the roofing word takes the nothing letter inside it

parts.note: slate is used for roof tiles
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Instructions for a builder working with live current and roof tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to separate it from others, to cut it off.

clue.text: Losing head, scatters nether garments

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: strews means scatters about

explanation.surface: Someone decapitated tosses trousers around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' takes the S from STREWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Trews are close-fitting tartan trousers, and nether garments is an old jokey term for trousers.

clue.text: Gismo buff always after good publicity and gain

indicators.note: after places the word for always behind the other three pieces

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is publicity
to get is to gain
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A gadget lover forever chasing good press and profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadgeteer is someone fascinated by gadgets, a fan of gismos.
